changes.comment: createHttpTransport takes an optional authProvider (McpOAuthClientProvider, the SDK's OAuthClientProvider under this package's name) for MCP servers that require OAuth 2.1. The interactive steps (state, saveCodeVerifier, redirectToAuthorization) run only inside connectMcpSession; on a later call, the SDK's background reconnect of the event stream, or close they are refused and the operation fails 'unauthorized'. redirectToAuthorization is also refused for a non-http(s) URL. The 'unauthorized' reason gains resourceMetadataUrl, the validated resource_metadata URL from the endpoint's WWW-Authenticate challenge. An OAuth error from the authorization server now classifies as 'unauthorized'. Failure messages no longer carry server-authored text: an 'unauthorized' failure, or one from an HTTP or OAuth error, reads as its kind and status (e.g. "unauthorized (HTTP 401)", "transport (HTTP 500)"), because a server may repeat a credential. Static headers are no longer sent to an authorization server on another origin.
